text: {"answer": "The evidence is mixed, so remote work does not clearly increase productivity across the board. A randomised call centre experiment found a 13 percent rise in completed calls among remote staff, attributed to a quieter environment and fewer breaks [remote_work#0]. Communication becomes more siloed after a remote transition, with slower information flow [remote_work#5], and software teams show weaker onboarding and mentoring that can depress output over time [remote_work#4].
